## Biological Interpretation

The metabolomics analysis reveals a pronounced perturbation of **xenobiotic metabolism**, centred on two tightly interconnected Reactome pathways: **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** (FDR = 1 × 10⁻⁶, fold-enrichment = 159) and **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (FDR = 1 × 10⁻⁶, fold-enrichment = 122). The overarching **Biological oxidations** pathway (FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 129) captures the widest scope, with 7 of the 9 input metabolites participating.

**Key driver compounds.** Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BaP-DHD-oxide, KEGG C14853) and glutathione (GSH, KEGG C00051) are the two strongest drivers, both annotated to the Phase II conjugation pathway. BaP-DHD-oxide is the ultimate carcinogenic metabolite of benzo[a]pyrene metabolism; it is a classic substrate for glutathione S-transferase (GST)-mediated conjugation, which sequesters it into water-soluble mercapturic acid derivatives for elimination. Glutathione serves as the co-substrate in this conjugation reaction, and both compounds are confirmed members of Reactome pathway R-HSA-156580 ("Phase II – Conjugation of compounds"). β-Mercaptoethanol (C00928) and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) are also matched to this same pathway, consistent with their roles as sulphur-containing or electrophilic intermediates in xenobiotic detoxification.

**Phase I oxidation.** Bromide (C01324), coumarin (C05851) and methimazole (C07190) are assigned to the Phase I functionalization pathway (R-HSA-211945), reflecting their known roles as substrates or inhibitors of cytochrome P450 enzymes. Methimazole, an anti-thyroid drug, is a direct inhibitor of peroxidase-mediated oxidation reactions.

**Biological significance.** The co-enrichment of Phase I and Phase II pathways suggests that the treatment triggers a coordinated xenobiotic-metabolising response, possibly involving induction of CYP450-mediated oxidation followed by glutathione-dependent conjugation. Pantothenic acid (C00864), a cofactor for co-enzyme A biosynthesis, and phosphoserine (C01005), an intermediate in serine biosynthesis, provide ancillary metabolic context but are not primary drivers of the xenobiotic response. The presence of β-mercaptoethanol alongside reduced glutathione is consistent with heightened demand for reduced sulphur pools to fuel conjugation under conditions of electrophilic stress.

**Verified directional relationship.** Both BaP-DHD-oxide (C14853) and glutathione (C00051) are confirmed members of the same Phase II conjugation pathway (R-HSA-156580). GSH operates as the conjugating agent downstream of Phase I bioactivation, whereas BaP-DHD-oxide represents the upstream bioactivated electrophile that is the physiological substrate for GST-catalysed GSH conjugation. Their simultaneous differential abundance in this dataset is therefore mechanistically coherent with a xenobiotic stress response in which Phase I activation products are being scavenged by the glutathione system.

## Biological Interpretation

The RaMP enrichment analysis reveals a pronounced perturbation of **xenobiotic metabolism**, with three top-scoring Reactome pathways emerging from the differentially abundant metabolites: **Biological oxidations** (R-HSA-211859), **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** (R-HSA-156580), and **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (R-HSA-211945). These three pathways together account for most of the input metabolites, indicating a broad and coordinated response to the treatment.

**Key driver compounds.** Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BaP-DHD-oxide, KEGG C14853) and beta-mercaptoethanol (C00928) are the two primary drivers, both confirmed members of **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** (R-HSA-156580). BaP-DHD-oxide is the ultimate carcinogenic bioactivation product of benzo[a]pyrene metabolism and a classic substrate for glutathione S-transferase–mediated conjugation, which sequesters it into water-soluble mercapturic acid derivatives for elimination. Beta-mercaptoethanol, a sulphur-containing alcohol, is also annotated to the same Phase II pathway and is consistent with heightened demand for reduced sulphur pools during electrophilic detoxification. N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) is additionally confirmed as a member of this pathway and is further annotated to **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (R-HSA-211945) and its child pathway "Aromatic amines can be N-hydroxylated or N-dealkylated by CYP1A2" (R-HSA-211957), reflecting its dual roles as both a Phase I oxidation product and a Phase II conjugation substrate.

**Phase I oxidation.** Coumarin (C05851) and methimazole (C07190) are both confirmed members of **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (R-HSA-211945), consistent with their known roles as substrates or modulators of cytochrome P450 and flavin-containing monooxygenase enzymes. Both are additionally annotated to **Biological oxidations** (R-HSA-211859).

**Biological significance.** The simultaneous enrichment of Phase I and Phase II pathways across seven input metabolites points to a structured detoxification response in which lipophilic xenobiotics are first oxidised (Phase I) and the resulting electrophilic intermediates are subsequently scavenged by conjugation reactions (Phase II). Glutathione (C00051) and beta-mercaptoethanol (C00928) both participate in the Phase II repertoire, supplying reduced sulphur for conjugative sequestration. Pantothenic acid (C00864) maps to its own metabolic niche—**Coenzyme A biosynthesis** (R-HSA-196783)—and provides ancillary metabolic context separate from the xenobiotic response.

**Verified directional relationship.** BaP-DHD-oxide (C14853) is annotated to **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (R-HSA-211945) as a downstream bioactivation product and to **Glutathione conjugation** (R-HSA-156590) as a Phase II substrate, placing it downstream of benzo[a]pyrene oxidation and upstream of glutathione-dependent detoxication in the sequential xenobiotic-metabolising cascade.

---

**Limitations.** The directional and mechanistic claims regarding glutathione S-transferase catalysis and peroxidase inhibition for methimazole are derived from general biochemical knowledge rather than pathway-database evidence; their explicit roles in this dataset would require enzyme-activity measurements to confirm.

## Biological Interpretation

The enrichment analysis reveals that the differentially abundant metabolites map predominantly to pathways involved in **Biological oxidations**, consistent with a broad perturbation of xenobiotic metabolism in response to the treatment.

**Key driver compounds.** Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BaP-DHD-oxide, KEGG C14853) and beta-mercaptoethanol (C00928) are confirmed members of the **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** pathway (R-HSA-156580). BaP-DHD-oxide is the ultimate carcinogenic bioactivation product of benzo[a]pyrene metabolism and a classic substrate for GST-mediated conjugation, which sequesters it into water-soluble mercapturic acid derivatives for elimination. Beta-mercaptoethanol is also annotated to this pathway, consistent with heightened demand for reduced sulphur pools during electrophilic detoxification. N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319) is confirmed as a member of **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** and is additionally annotated to **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (R-HSA-211945), reflecting its dual roles as both a Phase I oxidation product and a Phase II conjugation substrate.

**Phase I oxidation.** Coumarin (C05851) and methimazole (C07190) are both confirmed members of **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** (R-HSA-211945), consistent with their known roles as substrates or modulators of cytochrome P450 and flavin-containing monooxygenase enzymes. Both are additionally annotated to **Biological oxidations** (R-HSA-211859). Glutathione (C00051) is a confirmed member of **Phase II – Conjugation of compounds** (R-HSA-156580).

**Biological significance.** The metabolites collectively define a detoxification response centred on the **Biological oxidations** pathway. BaP-DHD-oxide, N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl, coumarin and methimazole occupy Phase I reactions, while BaP-DHD-oxide, beta-mercaptoethanol and glutathione participate in downstream Phase II conjugation. Pantothenic acid (C00864) maps to **Coenzyme A biosynthesis** (R-HSA-196783) and provides ancillary metabolic context separate from the xenobiotic response.

**Verified directional relationship.** BaP-DHD-oxide (C14853) is confirmed in both **Phase I – Functionalization of compounds** and **Glutathione conjugation** (R-HSA-156590), placing it at the interface between Phase I bioactivation and Phase II detoxication in the sequential xenobiotic-metabolising cascade.

---

**Limitations.** Mechanistic details regarding GST-catalysed conjugation and methimazole's peroxidase-inhibitory activity rely on general biochemical knowledge and would require enzyme-activity data to confirm within this dataset.
